# `kernel/attestation/CapabilityAttestation.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/attestation/CapabilityAttestation.js`

CapabilityAttestation.js — gates capability minting on descriptor attestation. Wraps engine/state's CapabilityRegistry/Capability.js (via the Phase 4 CapabilityNegotiator, kernel.protocol.capabilities — no parallel capability logic) and layers DescriptorHashStore on top so a capability is only minted for a tool whose descriptor hash matches the approved hash. The always-on Navi runtime requires explicit package or operator approval for every first-seen descriptor.

## Classes

### `class CapabilityAttestation`

| Method | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `constructor` | `constructor(kernel)` |  |
| `attestTool` | `async attestTool(appId, toolName, descriptor)` | Attest a tool descriptor and, if it passes, mint a capability for `appId` to invoke it. Returns `{ ok:false, reason:'descriptor-hash-changed' }` without minting anything if the descriptor changed since approval — callers (Phase 8's ApprovalCard) surface this as a re-review prompt. |
| `approve` | `async approve(name, descriptor)` |  |
| `approveSignedBuiltInRevision` | `async approveSignedBuiltInRevision(name, descriptor, proof)` | Kernel-only signed release handoff; never exposed as an application syscall. DescriptorHashStore binds the exact callable and deliberately treats package timestamps as audit data, never executable authority. |
| `revokeApproval` | `async revokeApproval(name)` |  |

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
